text:
Dana: Quick sync on API migration strategy. We need a low-friction path for integrators to move off the legacy POST-envelope shape without regressing latency for short embedding calls.

Ibrahim: Agreed. Two parallel mitigations: (A) conservative fast-path when client sends `X-Format: v1` header, (B) background rewriter that handles unknown shapes asynchronously.

Sophie: For (A) we should avoid any parsing work on the hot path: router inspects first 64 bytes and if header present, accept as-is. If absent, admission controller routes to rewriter.

Dana: Also add a tenant opt-in so we can flip fast-path per-tenant while monitoring. Product wants 60-day opt-in before removing legacy support per tenant.

eng-bot: created issue INC-4022 and posted initial heap samples: s3://heapdumps/compat/4301012345.hprof

Ibrahim: Implementation notes: use pooled buffers and copy-on-write for the async queue. Keep the inline detector O(1) and avoid full JSON unmarshal.

Sophie: Circuit-breaker: if async queue latency > 900ms or mem > 70% for 3m, reject with 429 + `X-Compat-Error: backpressure`. Log `compat_route=fast|admit|async|reject`.

Dana: Monitoring: p50/p95 latency, rewrite hit-rate, queue depth, per-tenant error rate, and sample payloads (anonymized).

Ibrahim: Timeline: 4d prototype (fast-path + detector), 3d async rewriter + telemetry, 2d console opt-in, 1d staged rollout. Parallelize where possible.

Sophie: Tests: unit for detector DFA, integration for queue overload, and end-to-end with SDKs. Add chaos test killing rewriter workers.

Dana: Owners: Ibrahim (detector & buffer pool), Sophie (replayer/async worker + tests), Claire (tenant UX + docs).

Claire: I'll draft console copy and the migration email. Recommend including sample curl and SDK snippet to add `X-Format` header.

Ibrahim: I'll open the PR for detector behind FF and include a small benchmark.

Dana: Good. Keep updates here and link PR/issue. :thumbsup:
